notes: All twelve tools are returned unconditionally by `list_tools` (server.py:321-456), so every tool is default-enabled.

No tool performs any network operation (no fetch/push/remote add), so there is no SINK anywhere in this server; all git invocations go through GitPython with argument-vector calls and explicit leading-'-' rejection, so no shell/flag-injection HOSTEXEC path is visible.
`git.Repo(repo_path)` at server.py:495 runs before the name match, so path validation applies uniformly to all tools.

`repo.index.commit` (server.py:129) and `repo.git.checkout` (server.py:220) can trigger repository hooks, but hooks reside in the user's own .git directory and are not transferred by clone, so HOSTEXEC is not attributed.

git_add.rationale: `git_add` stages files; paths are resolved and checked with `relative_to(repo_root)` so staging is confined to the repository working tree, and the tool returns only a fixed success string. No data leaves the host and no code is executed.

git_branch.rationale: `git_branch` returns `repo.git.branch` output including local branch names (private repo metadata, SECRET) and, with `branch_type` 'remote'/'all', remote-tracking branch names that are chosen by whoever controls the upstream (UNTRUSTED). `contains`/`not_contains` are guarded against leading '-'.

git_checkout.rationale: `git_checkout` runs `repo.git.checkout` on a ref validated by `rev_parse` and rejecting leading '-'; it mutates the local working tree but returns only a status string and reaches no external destination. Post-checkout hooks live in the user's own .git directory (not clone-transferred), so no HOSTEXEC is claimed.

git_commit.rationale: `git_commit` calls `repo.index.commit` which only writes a commit object into the local repository; there is no push, network call or externally readable destination, so no SINK. It returns only the commit hash, so no private data is surfaced.

git_create_branch.rationale: `git_create_branch` only creates a local ref via `repo.create_head` and returns a status string; leading '-' is rejected so no git flag injection. No exfiltration path and no private data returned.

git_diff.rationale: `git_diff` returns the patch text between the working tree and an arbitrary ref, which is private local repository content (SECRET). The target ref may be a remote-tracking branch or an imported/merged commit from a public upstream, so the returned patch text can contain third-party attacker-authored content (UNTRUSTED). Undetermined because the code does not constrain which refs may be diffed; the least restrictive reading is kept.

git_diff_staged.rationale: `git_diff_staged` returns the staged diff (`--cached`), exposing local file contents from the user's repository.

git_diff_unstaged.rationale: `git_diff_unstaged` returns `repo.git.diff` output, i.e. the literal contents of uncommitted local file changes, into the agent's context.

git_log.rationale: `git_log` returns commit hashes, author names and commit messages from the user's local repository (SECRET). Commit messages and author fields in a repository that tracks a public/third-party upstream are authored by other parties, so the text returned can carry attacker-controlled instructions (UNTRUSTED). Timestamps are guarded against leading '-' flag injection, so no argument-injection escalation.

git_reset.rationale: `git_reset` calls `repo.index.reset()`, a purely local index mutation returning a constant string; nothing is read out or sent anywhere.

git_show.rationale: `git_show` returns the full patch body of an arbitrary revision (`d.diff` decoded) plus author and message, i.e. private local repository file contents (SECRET). Any commit reachable in the repo may originate from a third-party/public upstream, making the returned diff and message text attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED).

git_status.rationale: `git_status` opens the caller-supplied `repo_path` with `git.Repo` and returns `repo.git.status()` output, exposing local working-tree state (file names, untracked paths) from the user's filesystem into the agent context. With no `--repository` restriction any repo path on the host can be read (`validate_repo_path` returns early when `allowed_repository is None`).

value_conditions.default: unset (repository is None → `validate_repo_path` returns immediately, no restriction)
value_conditions.effect: When set, `validate_repo_path` requires every `repo_path` argument to resolve inside the given repository, narrowing SECRET reads to that one tree; when unset, any git repository on the host filesystem can be opened and read.
`list_repos` enumerates repos from client roots, but it is never used by `call_tool`, so roots do not restrict which repository paths tools may open.
